# Incident Report: NetSupport RAT Infection — 2024-11-26

## Victim Host

| Field | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | **10.11.26.183** | Sole source of all malicious traffic in the capture |
| MAC | **d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b** | ARP replies and Ethernet source for 10.11.26.183 |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-B8TQK49** | NBNS name registration from 10.11.26.183 |
| Domain | NEMOTODES.HEALTH (DC: NEMOTODE-DC, 10.11.26.3) | NBNS, Kerberos realm, LDAP baseObject `DC=nemotodes,DC=health` |
| Logged-in user | **oboomwald** (Oliver Q. Boomwald) | Kerberos `CNameString=oboomwald`, LDAP query returning `CN=Oliver Q.. Boomwald,CN=Users,DC=nemotodes,DC=health` |

LAN scope: `10.11.26.0/24`, gateway/DC at `10.11.26.3`.

## Malware Family

**NetSupport RAT** (malicious repurposing of the legitimate NetSupport Manager remote-control client). **Attribution: signature-confirmed**, corroborated by protocol behavior.

- Suricata/ET alerts fired directly on the traffic: `ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity` (65 hits), `ETPRO TROJAN Malicious NetSupport Rat CnC Checkin` (2 hits), `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Checkin`/`Response`, `ET POLICY NetSupport GeoLocation Lookup Request` — all sourced from 10.11.26.183 to 194.180.191.64.
- HTTP User-Agent on every C2 request is literally `NetSupport Manager/1.3`.
- POST body payloads follow NetSupport Manager's own wire protocol verbatim: `POLL\nINFO=1\nACK=1\n` and `CMD=ENCD\nES=1\nDATA=<binary blob>`.
- Prior to beaconing, the host queried `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` and issued `GET /location/loca.asp` — NetSupport's own built-in geolocation check, run by the client at startup.

## Delivery Chain

1. `08:49:xx`–`08:50:11` — normal browsing (Bing, MSN, Windows/Office telemetry).
2. `08:50:11` — TLS connection to **classicgrand.com** (213.246.109.5).
3. `08:50:14` — TLS connection to **confirmsubscription.com** (52.8.34.0 / 13.56.30.207), immediately followed by TLS connections to **modandcrackedapk.com** (193.42.38.139) — repeated SNI hits through 08:50:40. This matches the ET signature `ZPHP Domain in DNS Lookup/TLS SNI (modandcrackedapk.com)`, indicating a fake cracked-software/APK lure site.
4. `08:50:45` — five minutes after the last contact with modandcrackedapk.com, the host performs the NetSupport geolocation lookup and then immediately begins C2 beaconing to 194.180.191.64:443. The payload delivery itself occurred inside the encrypted TLS session to modandcrackedapk.com — the executable/installer content is not recoverable in cleartext from this capture, so **no file name or SHA256 hash can be grounded in the traffic** for the initial dropper.

## Command-and-Control

- Beacon: `10.11.26.183` → **194.180.191.64:443** (plaintext HTTP over port 443, not TLS — flagged by `ET POLICY HTTP POST on unusual Port Possibly Hostile`), `POST /fakeurl.htm`, User-Agent `NetSupport Manager/1.3`.
- Beacon interval: roughly every 60 seconds, from 08:50:45 through 09:43:29 (end of capture) — continuous, persistent C2.
- Supporting infrastructure: `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` → 104.26.1.231, `GET /location/loca.asp` (legitimate NetSupport infrastructure, used here to geolocate the victim; benign NetSupport service, not itself malicious, but contextually part of the RAT's startup routine).

## Indicators of Compromise

| Type | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| c2_endpoint | **194.180.191.64:443** | 65+ POST /fakeurl.htm beacons matching ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity/Checkin signatures, from 10.11.26.183, 08:50:45–09:43:29 |
| domain | **modandcrackedapk.com** (193.42.38.139) | DNS query at 08:50:14 and repeated TLS SNI through 08:50:40; matches ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP Domain alert; delivery-chain site immediately preceding infection |
| domain | **confirmsubscription.com** (52.8.34.0, 13.56.30.207) | DNS query and TLS SNI at 08:50:14/08:50:15, part of the redirect chain into modandcrackedapk.com |
| domain | **classicgrand.com** (213.246.109.5) | DNS query and TLS SNI at 08:50:11/08:50:26, earliest hop in the redirect chain |
| url | **http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm** | C2 POST target, User-Agent `NetSupport Manager/1.3`, plaintext HTTP on port 443 |
| domain | geo.netsupportsoftware.com (104.26.1.231) | GET /location/loca.asp at 08:50:45, immediately before C2 beaconing starts (NetSupport client's own geolocation check) |

No file name or file hash could be grounded — the dropper/installer was delivered over TLS to modandcrackedapk.com and its contents are not visible in this capture.

## Benign Context (not IOCs)

Microsoft/Windows telemetry and update traffic (msftconnecttest.com, windowsupdate.com, smartscreen.microsoft.com, office.com/officeapps.live.com, login.live.com, MSN/Bing), Adobe update check (acroipm2.adobe.com, armmf.adobe.com), Google/CDN assets (fonts.googleapis.com, gstatic.com, maps.googleapis.com, code.jquery.com), CreateSend CDN (createsend1.com), Let's Encrypt OCSP (r10.o.lencr.org), SSDP/mDNS/LLMNR local discovery, and normal domain-joined AD/SMB/LDAP/Kerberos traffic to the DC at 10.11.26.3 (including EFSRPC and SMBv1/NTLMSSP signature hits, which are standard AD workstation-to-DC chatter here, not evidence of lateral movement).

## Incident Summary

Windows workstation DESKTOP-B8TQK49 (10.11.26.183, MAC d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b), logged in as domain user oboomwald in the NEMOTODES.HEALTH domain, was infected with **NetSupport RAT** after browsing through a redirect chain (classicgrand.com → confirmsubscription.com → modandcrackedapk.com, a fake cracked-software/APK lure). The RAT began beaconing to its C2 at 194.180.191.64:443 via HTTP POST to `/fakeurl.htm` roughly every 60 seconds and continued uninterrupted through the end of the capture (~53 minutes), giving the attacker persistent remote-control access to the host.
